title: Quantum-enhanced phase interrogation of a fiber-optic strain sensor
authors: Romain Dalidet, Marialuisa Capezzuto, Hugo Degert, Davide D'Ambrosio, Saverio Avino, Anthony Martin, Sebastien Tanzilli, Laurent Labonte, Paolo De Natale, Gianluca Gagliardi
abstract: Fiber-optic sensors enable high-sensitivity measurements of various physical parameters. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-enhanced interrogation of an all-fiber-optic Fabry-Perot resonator, employing entangled two-photon interference to probe directly strain-induced optical phase shifts. The resonator is interrogated by a narrow-linewidth laser that is frequency-locked to its resonance mode, thereby exploiting the cavity's inherent sensitivity to variations in the fiber length. To access the phase fluctuations transferred to the interrogation field due to external perturbations on the sensor, we implement an in-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer readout. This configuration allows the sensor to operate both with classical coherent light and with entangled photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Harnessing two-photon entangled states corresponding to an N = 2 NOON state, we experimentally demonstrate a reduction of the measurement noise below the standard quantum limit. These results provide clear evidence of the quantum advantage in enhancing fiber-optic sensors under practical constraints on optical power.
summary: The researchers implemented a quantum-enhanced sensing scheme for fiber-optic strain sensors using entangled photon pairs. By comparing measurements taken with classical light versus quantum light, they experimentally demonstrated that the measurement noise can be pushed below the standard quantum limit. This confirms the potential of quantum metrology to improve sensor sensitivity, especially when high optical power is impractical.
main_problem: The goal is to demonstrate a quantum-enhanced method for interrogating fiber-optic strain sensors to achieve measurement noise below the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL).
main_result: The experiment successfully showed that using entangled photon pairs (N=2 NOON state) reduces the phase noise below the shot-noise limit, demonstrating a quantum advantage for sensing under low-power constraints.
method: The setup uses an in-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) readout coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator interrogated by either classical coherent light or entangled photon pairs generated via SPDC.
model_or_system: The physical system is an all-fiber-optic sensor utilizing a Fabry-Perot resonator interrogated via an in-fiber MZI. The sensing mechanism relies on measuring strain-induced optical phase shifts ($\delta\phi$).
key_observables: Phase fluctuations ($\delta\phi$), Power Spectral Density (PSD) of phase noise, Allan deviation ($\sigma(	au)$), and coincidence counts of entangled photons.
important_parameters: Standard Quantum Limit (SQL), Heisenberg Limit (HL), strain magnitude, and low optical power regimes.
main_assumptions: The noise floor in the single-photon regime is assumed to be dominated by shot noise, allowing for a clear comparison with the quantum enhancement.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares single-photon readout (classical) against the SQL using time traces, Allan deviation, and PSD when strain is applied. Figure 3 compares phase readout using non-classical light, showing sub-shot noise performance in Allan deviation and PSD.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the classical sensing baseline by measuring noise approaching the SQL. It then introduces the quantum enhancement using entangled pairs, demonstrating a measurable reduction in noise below the SQL across various diagnostic plots (Allan deviation, PSD).
why_interesting: This work directly applies quantum optics principles (entanglement, NOON states) to a practical, macroscopic sensing platform (fiber optics), providing experimental validation of quantum metrology beyond the SQL in a low-power regime.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Experimental setup combining a PDH-locked fiber Fabry–Pérot resonator used as a strain sensor with an unbalanced fiber Mach– Zehnder interferometer (MZI) for phase readout. The interferometer can be operated with either classical light or non-classical light generated by a nonlinear generation unit (NLG): the NLG is formed by two cascaded nonlinear crystals for SPDC pumped with the 1560-nm laser. The MZI transmitted beams are detected with superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs).
